Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/FRAN-01 Lingua, letteratura e cultura francese

These analyses are conducted from both synchronic and diachronic perspectives, including through contrastive approaches. item.title: RTT: Ref. 6286_All. 8 - Textual, philological and ecdotic research on the Arthurian romance in France and Italy (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/FLMR-01 Filologie e letterature medio-latina e romanze

The project aims to study, from a textual, linguistic and ecdotic perspective, the development and dissemination of narrative structures and themes in the French Arthurian romance. Particular attention will be paid to the textual traditions within this medieval literary genre that incorporate the specific features of prophetic language, as well as to themes, historical settings and distinctive characters (particularly those who embody spiritual and moral development or narrative journeys of redemption). item.title: RTT: Ref. 6286_All. 9 - The literary text in historical tradition, encompassing philology, forms of rhetorical representation, and social impacts (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/ITAL-01 Letteratura italiana

The researcher will be expected to investigate texts from the Italian literary tradition through the specific lens of rhetorical genres, with particular attention to their philological features, as well as to the dissemination and circulation of literary works, identifying both elements of continuity and points of rupture within individual historical and cultural contexts. Alongside this primary area of research, a second line of inquiry may focus on the reception of these texts and their impact across different cultural horizons. item.title: RTT: Ref. 6286_All. 10 - Arabic Poetics, Rhetoric and Literary Theory: Philological and Comparative Perspectives from the Premodern to the Contemporary Period (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/STAA-01 Culture e lingue antiche e moderne dell'africa e dell'asia occidentale e centrale

The research will focus on the philological and literary study of texts written primarily in Classical Arabic and Modern Standard Arabic, with particular attention to the writing, criticism and reception of poetry and its relationship with other genres. Its main aim is to examine the connections between poetics, rhetoric, metre and literary forms, exploring how these take shape in theoretical writing and textual composition from the premodern to the contemporary period. item.title: RTT: Ref. 6347 - Translation, linguistic and cultural studies on translation processes in publishing and online discursive practices across the English-speaking world and Italy, with particular attention to gender, inclusion and accessibility studies (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Forlì
Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/ANGL-01 Anglistica e angloamericanistica

The researcher will conduct interdisciplinary research on translation processes in publishing and audiovisual media and on online discursive practices in the English-speaking world and Italy, integrating translation, linguistic and cultural studies with methodologies drawn from gender studies and critical discourse analysis. The research will focus in particular on literary texts, films and television series, as well as online hate speech, with attention to representations of gender and diversity and their circulation across languages and cultures. Field: Classics, philology, literature, art history / 10/FRAN-01 Lingua, letteratura e cultura francese

The researcher will carry out interdisciplinary research on translation processes between French and Italian in the publishing and cultural heritage contexts, combining Translation Studies and linguistic studies on the French language with gender studies, and intercultural studies, as well as research on accessibility and inclusion for people with disabilities. The research will focus particularly on texts that facilitate access to live performance and cultural heritage, children’s and young adult literature addressing gender issues, and texts produced in publishing contexts.
